source.title: Perturbation Probing: A Two-Pass-per-Prompt Diagnostic for FFN Behavioral Circuits in Aligned LLMs
source.authors: Hong-Liang Liu; Tung-Ling Li; Yuhao Wu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the single-direction refusal finding and presents causal results that refine its scope: its FFN-neuron ablation changes refusal formats, while harmful compliance remains rare and other safety behavior persists. It does not perform the original difference-in-means direction ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports causal results on refusal behavior using FFN-neuron ablation, patching, and restoration, so those results are included. Raw neuron rankings and values used only to select neurons are omitted. Results on sycophancy, language steering, and other non-refusal behaviors are not included. The paper’s cited results from other work are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. and calls its unembedding direction dF the 'unembedding-space analog' of the refusal direction. It never computes the harmful-minus-harmless direction, ablates it or adds it. Its interventions zero or patch selected FFN neurons, ranked by a perturbation × unembedding-coupling score, and its main metric is a first-token refusal-minus-affirmation logit gap. It does not show that these neurons write the Arditi direction. Its refusal results therefore concern a different construct: an FFN-neuron circuit for the refusal template. No version (V1–V8) is tested directly, so the findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ~50 FFN neurons (0.014%) in Qwen3-4B control the RLHF refusal template, not whether the model refuses. Under ablation, most responses become harm warnings and harmful compliance is 3/520. Safety topology is architecture-specific (Qwen FFN bottleneck, Llama skip-distributed, Gemma normalization-shielded), and the FFN/Skip ratio predicts ablation effectiveness. They also claim to localize the FFN sources of Arditi's direction but do not test that link.
record.recipe_differences: The paper ranks FFN neurons using a task-specific perturbation response and an unembedding-derived refusal–affirmation logit gap, then ablates or patches selected neurons. It does not use the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction or project that direction out at all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by prompt set (−64% on the identification prompts versus −56.6% on held-out HarmBench at 50 neurons), neuron count, and architecture. The authors also report that Gemma-2-9B has no safety-gap effect at any tested ablation dose.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen3-4B, ablating ~50 late-layer FFN neurons cuts the first-token refusal logit gap by 56–64% and changes the response template on 80% of 520 AdvBench prompts. Only 3/520 responses become harmful compliance, so substantive refusal and harm warnings persist.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small FFN-neuron set controls the refusal template (format), not whether the model refuses.

fits_no_version.finding: The effect of refusal-neuron ablation depends on architecture: Qwen3-4B −61%, Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-3-4B −39%, Gemma-2-9B and Gemma-4 0%. The FFN/Skip ratio predicts effectiveness (R²=0.81).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The FFN localization of refusal signal varies across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching harmful-prompt neuron activations into benign prompts induces refusal (6/6), and restoring the neurons on scrambled prompts recovers 107.7% of the gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A neuron-level sufficiency result for the refusal logit gap.

record.problems: The claimed residual-stream direction is not itself ablated or added. Most safety outcomes concern a first-token logit-gap proxy or response classifications, not a comprehensive capability evaluation. The main direct behavioral classification is on 520 AdvBench prompts; the held-out HarmBench dose-response reports the logit gap. The paper states no general-capability check for its refusal-neuron intervention.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted non-safety behavior circuits and their intervention results, cited findings from other papers, and neuron-ranking values used to select the intervention targets. Included only the reported safety/refusal outcomes relevant to V1.

untested.parts: The difference-in-means direction is never computed, ablated or added. Only FFN neurons and an unembedding token-difference direction are intervened on.
Harm warnings that persist after neuron ablation are suggestive only. Harmfulness representation is not separated from the refusal direction.
The base vs instruct gap (~+4 vs ~+16) concerns neurons and the logit gap, not the existence of a direction.

missing.what: Llama-3.2-3B behavioral flips under neuron ablation: 5/12 at K=50; 12/12 at K=1000 but about half of generations degraded. Gap drops are 47/66/83% at K=50/200/1000.
Gemma-4 shows 0% safety-gap effect under neuron ablation.
Injecting the language direction at α=50 drops the safety refusal gap by ~50%; at α≤30 it increases the gap.
Refusal-gap drops for gradient-ranked vs perturbation-ranked neurons across six models.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T5' for V1 is downgraded. The study never constructs or intervenes on the difference-in-means residual direction. Its dF is an unembedding token-difference vector, and its causal results are on FFN neurons, so the rows do not measure V1's named intervention. Verdicts against V1 (limits_scope) would conflate neuron ablation with direction ablation. Sycophancy and language results were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: It does not find the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction or project that direction out of every layer and position. Its ablations target selected FFN neurons, not the single residual-stream direction. It does not test general capability retention comprehensively.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-4B top-50 FFN-neuron ablation on the reported harmful-prompt evaluations
reader_labels.reason: The intervention substantially changes the refusal gap and response template, but harmful compliance remains 3/520 on AdvBench and the authors say the neurons control refusal format rather than whether the model refuses (r1, r13, r17-r20). This is neuron ablation, not removal of the claimed direction.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported effect is incomplete on Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-3-4B and absent on Gemma-2-9B, showing that this FFN-neuron intervention is architecture-dependent (r22-r24).
